messages:
lara-cs: Heads-up — LingoLabs (large localization customer) reported regressions after last Translate model rollout. They say Spanish prompts are returning long English explanations instead of concise Spanish translations, and Japanese responses are getting truncated. Customer is upset; asking for priority triage. :rotating_light:

lara-cs: Relevant details from the customer email:
- API: /v1/translate (hosted)
- Model: rwd-translate-v2 (promoted today)
- Rollout: canary -> 100% at ~1967889000 UTC
- Examples attached below

lara-cs: Example 1 (Spanish):
```
POST /v1/translate
Content-Type: application/json
Accept-Language: es-ES
{ "source": "en", "target": "es", "text": "Add a new payment method to the account settings." }
```
Customer saw response (unexpected English):
```
{ "translated_text": "To add a new payment method, go to Settings > Billing > Payment Methods and click \"Add\". Choose card or bank transfer..." }
```
They expected a short Spanish translation like: "Agregar un método de pago en Configuración."

anna-ml: Can you paste a few request IDs or full response bodies? Need examples to repro tokenization/language-detection flow. Also, did the customer set any prompt templates or post-processing?

lara-cs: Provided three request_ids: req_8f3a, req_8f3b, req_8f3c. Customer says they didn't change their client. Also seeing this for Chinese (zh) -> sometimes returns pinyin romanization instead of characters.

tony-oncall: Pinged. I'm seeing increased 95th latency for translate endpoints coincident with the rollout window (traces: https://internal/trace/tx/1967889). Could be a model variant mismatch or new tokenizer causing longer decode times -> beam/decoding switching.

kevin-runtime: Which quantization/kernel set did v2 use? The promotion job log shows rwd-translate-v2 built with tokenization-v3 and kernel set k-amp-7. v1 used tokenization-v2. Tokenization-v3 changes language-id heuristics.

lara-cs: Customer also sent a Japanese example that got truncated:
```
Request: {"source":"en","target":"ja","text":"Summarize onboarding steps for new users, keep under 40 words."}
Response: "新規ユーザーのオンボーディング手順：アカウント作成、確認、設定、チュートリアルを完了してから"
```
It ends mid-sentence and looks like decoding stopped early.

anna-ml: Ok — immediate plan: 1) Reproduce locally with tokenization-v3 & k-amp-7 using their request IDs, 2) run language-detection probe across top 25 locales, 3) check logits for early stopping/length penalty. I'll take this. Assigning to anna-ml.

anna-ml: Repro steps I ran in staging:
- Pulled rwd-translate-v2 image
- Used sample request body and Accept-Language headers from the customer
- Observed Spanish inputs sometimes trigger English completions when the language-detector confidence < 0.65
- Observed higher EOS probability spikes at token index ~18 for some Japanese prompts (causing truncation)
```
# quick repro snippet
curl -X POST https://staging/api/v1/translate -d '{"source":"en","target":"es","text":"Add a new payment method to the account settings."}' -H 'Accept-Language: es-ES'
```

kevin-runtime: Thanks — that points to tokenization-v3 behavior. We rolled tokenization-v3 to improve mixed-language segmentation, but looks like the calibration pushed language-id scores down for short prompts, which causes the model to mistakenly generate English. Also EOS calibration interacts with new length-penalty defaults in the runtime.

tony-oncall: Given customer impact and number of reports, recommend rollback of rwd-translate-v2 to v1 while we patch. I'll coordinate with deploy.

deploy-bot: ACTION: Rolling back rwd-translate-v2 -> rwd-translate-v1 on translate-cluster-3. Rollback started at 1967890500 UTC.

deploy-bot: STATUS: Rollback completed at 1967890560 UTC. All traffic now on rwd-translate-v1.

lara-cs: Customer reported that after rollback their Spanish translations returned to expected short Spanish text. They said Japanese truncation also stopped in their quick smoke tests. Customer asked for ETA on permanent fix.

anna-ml: Immediate mitigation: revert tokenization-v3 language-id changes (patch in progress) and add a confidence floor for language-detection on short inputs. Also adjusting EOS probability smoothing to avoid premature stops. Plan: patch + canary 5% tomorrow morning, run locale smoke tests.

kevin-runtime: Also adding a regression test to the Translate CI that exercises: short prompts (<=12 tokens), zh/ja/es locale headers, and checks for correct script/charset in outputs (no pinyin/romanization).

lara-cs: Thanks everyone — I'll send the customer a summary and let them know we're rolling a patched build through canary and will follow up with test results.

customer-alex: Thanks for quick rollback and updates. Would appreciate a heads-up before the next canary. Our SLA triggered a support credit flag; we'll discuss with your CS rep.

lara-cs: Noted. I'll coordinate a pre-canary notice moving forward. :thumbsup:
